pass_a_gloss: After recognizing our former evils—when we considered idols great and lofty, worshipping them and deeming them marvelous, though we now know they were all false and ineffective—we say, turning back: 'Indeed, the hills were false'; and we, having recognized the former heights and marvels. And perhaps, if we engage in philotechny, we will find the difference between the hills and mountains of the nations, which those who said, 'Behold, we shall be yours, for the Lord our God is He,' accuse as false, and the hills and mountains. What then is the difference between the mountains and hills of the nations, which, having recognized them, we say: 'Indeed, the hills were false and the power of the mountains'? This we say, having recognized the former. The things worshipped by the nations: some are worshipped as gods, others as heroes.
